summary: Fog-signal station on a headland near St. Shott's, Newfoundland: a Canadian fog alarm from 1910, a horn since 1957, staffed on rotation; the Coast Guard lists no light.

light.fog_signal: fog horn: blast 2 s, silence 8 s, blast 2 s, silence 8 s, blast 2 s, silence 38 s (CCG list)
light.note: No light characteristic is listed by the CCG for this station.

structures.type: white square building, brown roof, with a fog horn (CCG list; present site)
wooden fog-alarm building, dwelling house and outbuildings with a 3-inch diaphone plant, at Cape Freels (not the present site)
diaphone horn on the eastern head near St. Shotts

staffing.note: Two positions, rotational 7-day (CCG April 2010 data, Senate 2011); reduced to one staff member in 1981 (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Working Coast Guard fog-signal station, not remote; reachable by road (Senate 2011). No public visiting arrangement in the sources read.

visit.note: Working Coast Guard fog-signal station; no visitor arrangement in the sources read.

events.note: Canadian diaphone fog alarm on Cape Freels, put into operation 15 November 1910 (LighthouseFriends, quoting the notice to mariners); Department of Marine work completed in the year ending March 1911
Fog alarm moved to a spot down the slope from Cape Pine light (LighthouseFriends)
Manual horn, powered by bellows, worked by a hired operator; used until 1957
Department of Transport diaphone horn on the eastern head near St. Shott's
Station staff reduced to one person

keepers.name: Michael Myrick
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends: first keeper of the fog alarm, served until 1936. The 1911 Department of Marine keepers' list has 'Cape Freels Newfoundland Fog Alarm' with Myrick as keeper (OCR reads 'Michall Myrick'). LighthouseFriends treats the Cape Freels alarm as this station's first phase. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1911 keepers' list row for Cape Freels Newfoundland Fog Alarm was read on the page image (printed p. 235) and reads 'Michall Myrick'; the row is matched by row alignment and the image confirms it.

corrections.why: The CCG list gives 'St. Shotts Fog Signal Station' with a fog horn and no light characteristic.

The CCG list gives 46 37 25.0 N, 053 35 39.6 W for the fog signal station. The record's OSM point is about 300 m southwest of that position. LighthouseFriends gives 46.622443, -53.595977, which lies between them.

corrections.proposed: white square building with brown roof (fog horn), no tower
corrections.why: The CCG list describes a building with a horn, not a tower.

notes_for_editor: The 1882 wrecks (Gertrude, Eagle, Action), the 1883 Cabot inspection, the 1894 report and the 1946 and 1957 horns rest on LighthouseFriends alone. A Chronicling America search for 'Gertrude' with 'St. Shotts' in 1882-83 returned no matching page, so the wreck account is not confirmed by a contemporary newspaper. The Department of Marine 1911 report independently confirms the Cape Freels fog alarm, its diaphone and the keeper named there. The works table (printed p. 56, scan p. 63) lists 'Freels, cape' under the NOVA SCOTIA heading, so the Newfoundland location rests on the keepers' list heading and LighthouseFriends; the story says so. The keepers' list (printed p. 235, scan p. 242) is OCR: the Cape Freels row reads 'Michall Myrick' and was matched by row; the page image (checked 2026-10-28) confirms the name sits on the same row as the Cape Freels entry and gives an appointment date of 26 September 1910, which the story does not use because the OCR text does not carry it. Fact-check 2026-10-28 corrections: the current building (CCG) is not the 1910 Cape Freels building, so the 1910 date is now attached to the Cape Freels structure only; the 1946 operator is named as LighthouseFriends names him (service ended by 1957, before the post-1960 rule applies). Whether the 1957 horn stands on the 1910 site is unknown from the sources read; LighthouseFriends treats the stations as one line of succession (Cape Freels, Cape Pine, St. Shotts). Location: the CCG position (46 37 25.0 N, 053 35 39.6 W) and LighthouseFriends (46.622443, -53.595977) differ from the record's OSM point by about 300 m; the proposed correction is the CCG position. The CCG entry's '7.2' is a buoy item number, not a height, so no height is recorded. Keepers from 1957 onward are named only in their public role, as LighthouseFriends lists them. No photos added. Chapter shape fixed 2026-10-28: the 1882 wrecks now sit under Storms, wrecks and rescues; the 1966 power and 1981 staff cut sit under After the keepers.
